instruction: Using all relevant parts of the text, describe the sequence from proposal submission through policy issuance and CIS provision, including the timing constraints and the conditions for premium payment and risk cover commencement.
response: The text states that the proposer must ensure all required details are provided before signing the proposal/enrolment form (for group insurance). While filling the proposal form, the prospect must provide nominee details, and nomination is mandatory to facilitate claim payment on death; nomination can be changed anytime during the policy term. Premium is required to be paid only after the insurer communicates acceptance of the proposal, and risk cover commences only after receipt of premium (with no premium/proposal deposit along with the proposal form except for policies issued based on declaration of good health, where risk cover commences immediately on receipt of premium). The insurer processes the proposal with speed and efficiency; if further details/clarifications are needed, they should be called for in one-go within 7 days from receipt, and the prospect should provide information at the earliest. The insurer must take a decision within 7 days; on acceptance it promptly communicates the decision with the premium payable and provides coverage from the date of receipt of premium, while on non-acceptance it informs the prospect within 7 days with reasons. After acceptance, the prospect is referred to as the policyholder or insured; the insured is the person whose risks are covered, and the policyholder is the person in whose name the policy is issued. The insurer issues the insurance policy in electronic form on acceptance and upon receipt of premium; choice for availing a physical policy document must be sought in the proposal form, and electronic policies are also issued in physical form if requested by the policyholder. Electronic policies are digitally signed. Within 15 days of acceptance, insurers furnish without additional charge: the policy document, copy of the proposal form, Customer Information Sheet (CIS), and medical reports if applicable. CIS is defined as a statement provided with the policy document in simple words, and it must be provided with every policy (individual and group members). CIS includes details such as type of insurance, sum insured, coverage, exclusions, sub-limits, deductibles, co-payment, waiting periods, and important items like Free Look Period, Policy Renewal, IVIigration, Portability and Moratorium Period, plus claims procedure and grievance redressal mechanism including Insurance Ombudsman contact details. Acknowledgment of CIS in physical or digital must be obtained from the policyholder, and on request CIS is made available in regional language.

instruction: Using all relevant parts of the provided text, describe the complete sequence of actions and conditions for (1) lodging a complaint, (2) resolution and tracking, (3) escalation to the Insurance Ombudsman including the claim amount condition and the available submission methods, and (4) what happens regarding compliance timelines, penalties, and the exception if the insurer appeals—ensuring you include the specific time limits, URLs, and penalty amount stated.
response: A policyholder/beneficiary not satisfied can lodge complaints directly with the insurer or the distribution channel including TPA or with both, using one of these modes: nearest branch, letters or email, insurer's website, or designated call centre. They can also register on-line at IRDAI's Bima Bharosa (https://bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in/). Insurers must integrate their grievance portal with Bima Bharosa and use real-time mirroring to keep grievance databases synchronized. On receipt, the complainant must get acknowledgement immediately, and insurers must resolve within 14 days, including reasons for not accepting with reference to relevant policy terms and conditions. The complainant can track status by logging-in to Bima Bharosa, the insurer's grievance portal, or via the insurer's call centre. If not satisfied with the insurer’s resolution, unresolved/partially resolved complaints can be escalated to the Insurance Ombudsman of concerned jurisdiction if the claim amount is up to Rs. 50 lakhs. A policyholder can take up the matter without any charge/fee in person, online at https://cioins.co.in/Complaint/Online, or in writing by post or by email with complete details. Ombudsman name/address details are available in the policy document and in the insurer’s resolution letter, and also at https://cioins.co.in/Complaint/Online. The insurer must comply with the Ombudsman award within 30 days of receipt; if not honoured within 30 days, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day is payable to the complainant for each day of delay, in addition to penal interest under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017. The penalty provision does not apply if the insurer appeals against the award within 30 days; in that case, due intimation must be sent to the Policyholder.
